newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs seen consolidating, long end curve flattens.
newsitem.headline: OLOs seen consolidating, long end curve flattens.

text.p: Belgian linear bond futures opened lower on Tuesday, following Monday's close for Whit Monday, as investors hesitated to open long positions ahead of the U.S. FOMC meeting and the OLO exchange auction.
Economists are split on whether the Federal Reserve's policy-making committee would vote to hike rates again. The previous 25 bp rate hike was decided on March 25.

Dealers expected the Belgian market to consolidate in the days ahead, tracking Bunds and with an OLO/Bund yield spread around the current level of nine basis points. Some also expect a further flattening of the long end of the yield curve.

"I expect the long end of the curve, 10-20 years, will continue the flattening move which started Friday. In the U.S. the 10-20 spread is virtually flat, while in Europe it is relatively wide," said BBL trader Gunter Fluyt.
He added he also thought there was too much fear of inflation discounted in the long end of the curve.

Dealers expect good volume in the exchange auction later today. The Treasury is offering OLOs 27 (4.00 pct, Jan 2000), 25 (5.00 pct, March 2001), 6 (9.00 pct, March 2003), 19 (6.50 pct, March 2005) and 26 (6.25 pct, March 2007) against OLO 4 (9.25 pct, Jan 1998).
